title: Etiquette
intro: Download: Google Translate offline + show screen if stuck.

tables.caption: Daily Norms (Everywhere)
rows: Small bow or nod; arigatou gozaimasu
Walk on tatami with outdoor shoes
Leave coins — staff may chase you
Flash in dark halls; drone without permit

tables.caption: Essential Phrases (Romanji → Meaning)
rows: ありがとうございます
英語メニューありますか？

tables.caption: Train & Shinkansen Etiquette
rows: Avoid unless marked open; yield to elderly
Front pack or between feet in rush hour
OK on Shinkansen; avoid strong smells on commuter metro
Sit in unreserved or reserved seat on ticket — not Green unless paid
Last trains ~midnight Tokyo; plan taxi or stay near Dotonbori

tables.caption: Temple & Shrine Etiquette
rows: Rinse left hand, right hand, mouth at chozuya
2 bows, 2 claps, 1 bow at main hall
Incense, single bow; no clap at some
Coin in box; no required amount

tables.caption: Dining Etiquette (Solo)
rows: Don't stick upright in rice; don't pass food chopstick-to-chopstick
Don't pour over rice bowl at kaiseki
Order drink first; shared plates normal even solo (small portions)
Ask chef omakase or point; eat piece within moment
No double-dipping sauce (one bite per dip rule)
Eat at store counter or park bench — not walking

tables.caption: Ryokan / Onsen (Takayama Night)
rows: Wash body completely before entering tub
Some public baths restrict — ryokan private bath often OK; ask front desk
Never in tub water; fold on head or edge
Arrive on time for kaiseki seatings

tables.caption: Solo-Specific
rows: Golden Gai: cover charge + one drink; read sign outside
Very safe; standard urban awareness at night
Takkyubin — don't block train aisles with giant suitcase
Solo still waits full queue — no "just one person" cut

bullets.heading: Regional Notes
items: Fast-paced; stand left on escalators (Tokyo) — right in Osaka/Kyoto (verify signs — follow locals).
Slower pace; greet shopkeepers entering/leaving stores.
Morning market: Don't block stalls with large bag.
Shirakawa-go: Stay on paths; private homes are not museums.
Most formal — softer voice in residential lanes (Ninenzaka, Gion).
Geiko/Maiko: No touching, no blocking; photography often prohibited in alleys.
Rickshaw: Negotiate route/time; not required for short hills.
Casual, jokey culture — OK to chat with counter chefs.
Comedy loudness in Dotonbori — still no litter.
Kuidaore ("eat till you drop") — sample sizes, not waste.

bullets.heading: What Will Surprise You (Good)
items: Staff bow when you leave convenience store.
Exact change trays at registers — don't hand cash directly if tray present.
Police helpful for lost items — report at koban if needed.

bullets.heading: What Will Surprise You (Avoid)
items: Assuming English everywhere — patience + translate app.
Talking on elevator — quiet box culture.
Opening taxi doors — driver auto-opens rear left.

train.caption: Transit & Street Culture
rows: Walk steady — bikes flow around you (Vietnam)
Use DiDi (China) and Grab (Vietnam) — avoid airport street taxis

temple.caption: Temple & Shrine Etiquette
rows: Shoulders/knees covered; no flash where signed
Remove shoes; borrow sarong if offered
Ask when unsure; respect 禁止拍照 signs

footer: China: no tipping · Vietnam: soft tip 10–15% at sit-down restaurants.
